abstract: Computational mapping of extracellular-vesicle cargo to recipient-cell receptors can prioritize experiments, but donor non-independence, database bias, transcript thresholds, and clinical confounding can inflate inference. We developed a donor-aware cross-modal workflow and applied it to 14 human meniscus single-cell RNA-sequencing libraries from 13 donors (GSE220243). Donor-by-state pseudobulk models were combined with directional, full-subunit OmniPath verification, human mesenchymal stromal cell extracellular-vesicle (MSC-EV) protein evidence from ExoCarta, continuous receptor-complex bottleneck scores, 15 threshold-prevalence settings, 1000 stratified donor bootstraps, and 5000 expression- and ligand-degree-matched permutations. External evidence comprised PRJCA008120 marker sets, covariate-adjusted GSE98918 transcriptomics, and published PXD042122 proteomics. Quality control retained 86,953 singlets; after excluding one uncertain cluster, 17 annotated states remained, of which 13 were donor-eligible. Evidence gating reduced 69 legacy hypotheses to 38 cargo-receptor-pathway combinations involving eight ExoCarta-retained candidate cargos. No receptor-panel enrichment survived multiplicity correction in the matched-null audit. Relative to the reference setting, 194 of 195 state-setting comparisons retained identical top-10 receptor sets, and 96 of 442 receptor-state contexts remained top-10 in every bootstrap. In GSE98918, 1995 genes were significant before covariate adjustment, whereas none reached transcriptome-wide false-discovery-rate significance after adjustment. Four prespecified receptor components were quantified in PXD042122; ITGAV was lower in end-stage osteoarthritis medial meniscus (published q = 0.045). This workflow yields a reproducible, evidence-bounded shortlist of transcript-defined receptor contexts. It does not establish EV delivery, receptor activation, age-independent disease effects, or therapeutic efficacy.
